rationale: Both recompute the affected cells in topological order using a depth-first search, and both expose value as a read-only property. A cleanly separates the two phases: it records the old values, recomputes every dependent, and only then fires callbacks for cells whose value differs from the previous stable state. That matches the requirement to notify on stable-state changes, so callbacks never see a partly updated system. B fires each callback inside _recompute, before the rest of the graph has settled, so a callback that reads other cells could observe stale values. B's shared Cell base class is a nice structural touch, and its propagate comment is helpful, but its traversal duplicates the visited check before the recursion. On balance A's two-phase propagation is more robust and just as clear.
